Here’s a quick rundown of the public‑holiday “long weekends” (i.e., holidays that fall on a Friday or Monday, creating a three‑day weekend) that occurred in Canada during 2023.  (Note that some holidays are provincial only; the table below lists the nationwide ones first, followed by a few key provincial examples.)

| Date (2023) | Holiday | Province(s) Observed | Notes |
|-------------|---------|----------------------|-------|
| **January 1** (Sunday) | New Year’s Day | All provinces & territories | Falls on Sunday → observed on Monday, Jan 2 |
| **January 16** (Monday) | Family Day (Alberta, Saskatchewan, Ontario) | AB, SK, ON | Creates a long weekend in those provinces |
| **February 20** (Monday) | Louis Riel Day (Manitoba) | MB | Long weekend in Manitoba |
| **March 17** (Friday) | St. Patrick’s Day (Ontario) | ON | Long weekend in Ontario |
| **April 7** (Friday) | Good Friday | All provinces & territories | Creates a long weekend everywhere |
| **May 22** (Monday) | Victoria Day | All provinces & territories | Creates a long weekend everywhere |
| **June 19** (Monday) | National Indigenous Peoples Day (BC) | BC | Long weekend in British Columbia |
| **July 1** (Saturday) | Canada Day | All provinces & territories | Falls on Saturday → observed on Monday, July 3 |
| **September 18** (Monday) | Labour Day | All provinces & territories | Creates a long weekend everywhere |
| **October 9** (Monday) | Thanksgiving (Canada) | All provinces & territories | Creates a long weekend everywhere |
| **November 10** (Friday) | Remembrance Day (observed on Monday, Nov 13) | All provinces & territories | Creates a long weekend everywhere |
| **December 25** (Monday) | Christmas Day | All provinces & territories | Creates a long weekend everywhere |
